profile.label: Documentation profile
profile.help:
Markdown export and default documentation focus follow this choice.

Every run still generates all three HTML profiles (admin, user, onboarding). User/Onboarding AI runs when an AI provider is configured — not controlled by this dropdown.

language.label: Documentation language
language.help: Headings, labels, and fixed wording in Admin, User/Family, and Onboarding HTML exports and in Markdown follow this language (English / German / French). Adapter names, state ids, and room strings from ioBroker stay unchanged.

autoGenerateOnStart.label: Generate documentation on adapter start
autoGenerateOnStart.help: If enabled, documentation is queued each time the adapter starts (runs in the background; the instance can show green before it finishes). If disabled, a run still happens once after an update when the built-in HTML renderer version no longer matches info.templateVersion. Check the log for "Documentation generated via startup" and state info.lastTrigger.

autoGenerateOnEvents.label: Generate documentation on adapter changes
autoGenerateOnEvents.help: If enabled, documentation regenerates when adapters are installed, removed, or enabled or disabled. 30 s debounce groups bursts of changes into one run after a short quiet period.

autoGenerateInterval.label: Scheduled interval (hours)
autoGenerateInterval.help: Optional timer: regenerate every X hours, independent of start and adapter-change options above. 0 = no scheduled runs (events and start still work). Example: 24 = about once per day.

readLiveStates.label: Read live state values (opt-in)
readLiveStates.help: If enabled, current values for selected state roles are read and shown in User/Onboarding room cards and the Admin device table (badges next to device names). Includes e.g. temperature, blinds (level.blind), dimmers, lights (switch.light), outlets (switch/plug), humidity, power metrics, locks, door/window/contact, motion, alarm. Room members may be channels or devices — matching child states are found automatically. Very custom or empty roles are skipped.

confirm.title: Generate documentation
confirm.text: Start documentation generation now? This may take a few seconds.

projectName.label: Project name
projectName.help: Name of the ioBroker project or installation. Shown in exports and notifications. Example: Demo home or Musterhaus Schulweg (use fictional labels in public screenshots).

projectDescription.label: Project description
projectDescription.help:
What the installation covers in one or two sentences (e.g. family home: heating, lighting, security). Shown in exports as the short system summary.

Counts toward the optional documentation setup score when that check is on (Advanced tab — minimum length).

manualContact.label: Contact person
manualContact.help: Who manages this system? e.g. 'Max Mustermann, Telegram @max' - shown so guests and family know who to ask

additionalNotes.label: General notes
additionalNotes.help: Anything that doesn't fit elsewhere: e.g. 'Backup runs every Sunday, server is in the basement' — same field for maintenance windows, NAS paths, or hardware quirks.

guestHelpNote.label: Help & emergencies (guests/family)
guestHelpNote.help: Who to call, what to try if something fails, where the fuse box is — your words only; nothing is invented automatically.

homeRoutinesNote.label: Routines & automations (your words)
homeRoutinesNote.help: Describe in everyday language what often runs by itself (lights, heating, blinds). Shown near the script list; complements technical script names.

ownerPlaybookNote.label: How we run this home (your playbook)
ownerPlaybookNote.help: Step-by-step or bullet notes only you maintain: typical order of doing things, what must be done, what guests or family must not change (your words; nothing is invented automatically). Shown as its own section in family and guest docs.

manualMermaidDiagram.label: Mermaid diagram (optional)
manualMermaidDiagram.help:
Optional Mermaid diagram you write yourself (flowchart, sequence, …). HTML exports: With `@mermaid-js/mermaid-cli` installed on the ioBroker host (optional npm dependency), diagrams are rendered to embedded SVG during generation — works in offline `file://` copies without network. Without the CLI the export uses `<pre class="mermaid">` and loads Mermaid 10.9.1 from jsDelivr when you open the page in a browser (online).

When all diagrams are embedded as SVG, the export no longer loads jsDelivr (the script is only injected if a `<pre class="mermaid">` remains).

Markdown always emits a ```mermaid source fence (not pre-rendered). Hide your manual diagram in User/Onboarding with chapter id `mermaid` (`mermaidAuto` is only for the optional auto-host diagram below). Very long input is truncated. Tip: `flowchart LR` uses horizontal page width; `flowchart TB` (default) stacks top-to-bottom.

autoMermaidHostGraph.label: Auto host topology diagram (Mermaid)
autoMermaidHostGraph.help: When enabled, adds a second Mermaid diagram in HTML: adapter instances grouped by ioBroker host (helps in multihost setups). Instance node count is capped (next setting); not a full wiring graph. In User/Onboarding hide lists, use `mermaidAuto` to hide only this auto diagram (`mermaid` hides your manual diagram above). Same HTML embedding as manual Mermaid: embedded SVG when the CLI runs on the host, otherwise `<pre>` + jsDelivr in the browser.

autoMermaidHostGraphMaxNodes.label: Max instances in auto topology diagram
autoMermaidHostGraphMaxNodes.help: Maximum adapter instance nodes in the auto-generated diagram (8–200, default 40). Hosts are still shown; instances are chosen round-robin across hosts when there are more than this limit.

troubleshootWifiHint.label: Quick: Wi-Fi / network
troubleshootWifiHint.help: One line, e.g. guest Wi-Fi name or where a repeater is — optional.

troubleshootPowerHint.label: Quick: power / fuses
troubleshootPowerHint.help: One line, e.g. where the electrical panel is — optional.

troubleshootWaterHint.label: Quick: water shutoff
troubleshootWaterHint.help: One line, e.g. where to turn off main water — optional.

troubleshootExtraHint.label: Quick: other
troubleshootExtraHint.help: One more short line (alarm code location, key box, etc.) — optional.

adapterNotes.label: Adapter notes
adapterNotes.help: Add a human-readable note for specific adapters (shown in all profiles). Table row example: adapter hue — note Living room scenes — wall switch overrides.

roomNotes.label: Room notes
roomNotes.help: Add a human-readable note for specific rooms (shown in User and Onboarding profiles). Example: room Kitchen — note Gas shutoff — left of sink.

onboardingGuestShowScriptNames.label: Onboarding guest view — list internal JavaScript file names

onlyEnabledInstances.label: Only document enabled instances
onlyEnabledInstances.help: When enabled, disabled adapter instances are omitted from instance lists in every export (HTML and Markdown).

hideInstanceDetailsInMarkdown.label: Hide instance details in markdown
hideInstanceDetailsInMarkdown.help: When enabled, Markdown skips per-instance detail blocks and keeps overview-style sections. HTML exports still list instances as usual.

maxDocumentedInstances.label: Maximum documented instances
maxDocumentedInstances.help: After the optional enabled-only filter, only the first N instances in discovery order are kept (0 = unlimited). Applies to HTML and Markdown.

maxStoredFiles.label: Maximum stored documentation files
maxStoredFiles.help: How many timestamped file sets to keep (per type: .md, .html, .json). Oldest are deleted automatically. 0 = use default (3).

baseUrl.label: ioBroker base URL (optional)
baseUrl.help: Used for the info.htmlUrl state and bookmark/QR targets. Include host and port, e.g. http://192.168.1.100:8081 or https://iobroker.home:443 — no trailing slash. Protocol is optional. Leave empty for auto-detection (may fail in Docker).

maintenanceScoreCheckBaseUrl.label: Maintenance score include base URL check
maintenanceScoreCheckBaseUrl.help: Maintenance score base URL check help

maintenanceScoreMinDescriptionChars.label: Maintenance score min description length
maintenanceScoreMinDescriptionChars.help: Maintenance score min description length help

maintenanceScoreUnassignedWarnAt.label: Maintenance score unassigned warn at
maintenanceScoreUnassignedWarnAt.help: Maintenance score unassigned warn at help

notifyEnabled.label: Send notification after documentation generation
notifyEnabled.help: If enabled, the messaging instance below sends a message after each successful documentation run (manual Generate or the same automatic triggers as generation).

notifyInstance.label: Messaging adapter instance
notifyInstance.help: Adapter instance that delivers the notification, e.g. telegram.0 or pushover.0. Must be installed and enabled in ioBroker; use the exact instance id from Objects / Instances.

notifyTarget.label: Recipient (optional)
notifyTarget.help: Telegram username, Pushover device, or email address - leave empty for adapter default. Examples: Telegram @nickname, email ops@example.com, Pushover device phone.

notifyMessage.label: Custom message template (optional)
notifyMessage.help: Use {project}, {summary}, {version}, {trigger} as placeholders. Leave empty for default message. Example: {project} — documentation updated ({trigger}). {summary}

aiProvider.label: AI provider
aiProvider.help: Ollama recommended: runs locally, no data leaves your network. Cloud providers send adapter/room/script names to external servers.

options.label: Groq — US, free tier (data may be used for training)
Anthropic Claude — paid, no training on data

aiModel.label: AI model (optional)
aiModel.help: Leave empty for default. Ollama: llama3.2 / gemma3. Mistral: mistral-small-latest. Groq: llama-3.3-70b-versatile. Anthropic: claude-haiku-4-5-20251001

aiApiKey.label: API key
aiApiKey.help: Mistral: console.mistral.ai | Groq: starts with gsk_... | Anthropic: starts with sk-ant-... | Ollama: leave empty

aiRequestTimeoutSeconds.label: AI request timeout seconds (optional)
aiRequestTimeoutSeconds.help: Maximum wait for one LLM HTTP request. Default 300. Each generation uses several calls (user, onboarding, sometimes a German polish pass). Increase for slow local models on CPU (e.g. 480 or 600 for llama3.1:8b on NAS). Range 30–900.

aiTemperatureUser.label: AI temperature — user profile (optional)
aiTemperatureUser.help: Sampling temperature for resident-facing AI text. Leave empty for the provider default. Typical range 0–2 (Ollama, Groq, Mistral); Anthropic accepts 0–1 (values above 1 are clamped). Lower ≈ steadier wording; higher ≈ more variation — tune after testing.

aiTemperatureOnboarding.label: AI temperature — onboarding (optional)
aiTemperatureOnboarding.help: Sampling temperature for guest/onboarding AI text. Same rules as user profile. The German Sie polish pass uses a fixed low temperature and ignores this field.

aiAnalyzeScriptSources.label: AI explain JavaScript scripts (opt-in)
aiAnalyzeScriptSources.help: Sends sanitized script source to the same AI provider to add short plain-language explanations in User/Onboarding docs. Lines matching common secret patterns are redacted first; still review before enabling on production systems.

aiMaxScriptCharsForAi.label: Max characters of script source per KI call
aiMaxScriptCharsForAi.help: How many characters of each script (after redaction) are sent to the model; longer sources are truncated. Default 12000. Lower to speed up or fit small context; raise only if your model and timeout allow. Range 2000–100000. State info.aiScriptSourceProgress shows e.g. 5/12 while processing.

confirm.title: Cancel script KI
confirm.text: Stop the optional per-script KI pass? The request that is already running may still finish; further scripts will not be started. (The main user/onboarding KI calls run before this phase.)
